//: COLD START, tactical. From the main menu of a game that has never played anything, load ANY plot scene as a real playable mission - no campaign, no save, no hand-setup.
//needs: NOTHING. It works on a game sitting at the HomeScreen; if a level is already open it closes it first (see `to-menu`).
//scene: `scene` is a MapPlotDef's own SceneReference.SceneName - e.g. ALN_PLT_Nest_48x48_A for ALN_PLT_Nest_48x48_A_PlotDef. `find` a *_PlotDef and read Scene.SceneName off it for any of the 213 plots. The scene must be in build settings; 876 of them are, and every plot checked so far is one (loadmap throws ConsoleCommandException otherwise, MapPlot.cs:334-337).
//lever: `loadmap` (MapPlot.cs:320-366) assembles the TacticalGameParams itself off SharedData.TacticalLevelDef and hands PhoenixGame.FinishLevel a LoadLevelGameResult (:365). MenuCrt then branches on the params TYPE into TacticalGameCrt (PhoenixGame.cs:514-523). No mod code and no new bridge verb.
//menu-only: loadmap is MENU-ONLY. Called inside a tactical level, TacticalGameCrt (PhoenixGame.cs:573-583) casts the result to TacticalGameResult and throws InvalidCastException - hence the phase gate below, which is a hard failure and not a warning.
//tags: ponytail: loadmap's `params string[] tags` (plot/parcel tag filter) is NOT exposed - the plan engine cannot splice an array var into a console arg list, and args must stay flat (Protocol.cs:190-193). Add the literals to the `load` step if a run needs them.

steps.//: THE GATE, computed rather than asked of the caller: FinishLevelAndGoToLobby AT the menu makes MenuCrt take a QuitGameResult it has no branch for and throw (PhoenixGame.cs:492-495), so the lobby call must not fire when there is nothing to leave.

steps.//REFUSAL: A LIVE GEOSCAPE CANNOT BE LEFT FROM HERE, so this plan refuses rather than wedging the game. Measured 2026-08-28: FinishLevelAndGoToLobby out of a running geoscape (and `load_game`, which takes the same road) tears the level down while GeoscapeView keeps updating - UIStateVehicleSelected.UpdateState then NREs every frame inside StateStack.Update, MenuCrt's HomeScreen never reaches Playing, and the process is stuck at phase:menu with level:null until it is killed. GeoscapeView.ResetViewState first does NOT help; its SwitchToState is applied on a later frame that never comes. Quit the campaign from the in-game pause menu, or restart the process. Tactical is fine and is exercised below.

steps.//: The engine has no `not`; Object.Equals(false, x) is the idiom the other plans use.
PhoenixGame.cs:284. The 0 is MenuEnterReason.None - the binder matches arity exactly, so the default cannot be omitted.

TWO waits, and the second one is what the first run of this plan was missing. `phase` flips to menu the moment the TacticalLevelController is gone - the HomeScreen level itself is not up yet, and a loadmap issued in that gap sets _levelResult before MenuCrt starts reading it (PhoenixGame.cs:262-266,481-490): the pulse is swallowed and the game sits at the menu forever. Measured: 123 ms to `phase:menu`, and the load then timed out at 420 s.

The HomeScreen level is REALLY up. While it loads @level is null and the call errors, and an error satisfies neither polarity (Plan.cs:268-272), so this waits rather than passing. Safe on the already-at-the-menu path too, where it is true on the first poll.
Two waits, because they are two different facts. `phase` says the TacticalLevelController exists; `ready` is HasAnyTurnStarted, which is when the mission is actually driveable.
WHAT THE MISSION ACTUALLY BECAME. A load that 'succeeded' into an empty map is the failure this reports.
ONE PASS PER FACTION. The engine has no loop variable, so the accumulator's own Count is the index - the same trick spawn-squad.json uses for its `while` guard.

TacticalFaction.Actors is a LAZY iterator over the map (TacticalFaction.cs:68), so it has no Count of its own - Enumerable.Count walks it once and answers with a number instead of a page of projected actors.

finally.//: NO lobby call here. A plan that dumped the player back to the menu on its own timeout would throw away a mission that may have loaded a second later, and `loadmap` leaves nothing behind that needs undoing - the level owns everything it built.
